2.8.1 INTRODUCTION TO ANGIOSPERM The term angiosperms (Greek; angios-enclosed, sperma-seed) means ‘enclosed seed’ because the ovules or seeds are enclosed within a hollow ovary. They are the most common among land plants and form the largest group of plant kingdom. These plants are found almost everywhere in all possible type of habitat and climate and may be annual, biennial or perennial herbs, shrubs, trees and climbers. Angiosperms show great diversity both in vegetative and in reproductive structures. They show variation in life span, size, form, habit, etc.

2.8.2 MORPHOLOGY OF ANGIOSPERM Morphology is the study of forms and features of different plant organs like roots, stems, leaves, seeds, fruits etc. The body of a typical angiosperm is differentiated into an underground root system and an aerial shoot system. The morphology of angiosperms is described in following headings:
1. Root 2. Stem 3. Leaves 4. Inflorescence
